review_notes:
I read the whole file and checked Mathlib for existing quotient-idempotent lemmas. I found none.

The most visible repetition is the same four-line `rw [IsIdempotentElem, ← map_mul, ← sub_eq_zero, ← map_sub, Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem]` block. It proves "`z*z - z ∈ I` implies `mk z` is idempotent". It appears three times: `hidem` (lines 51–54), `h1` (71–74) and `h2` (75–78). This is routine unfolding. A shared lemma would save only about eight lines and would be a thin wrapper around `Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem`, so I did not report it.

The two final bullets of `solution` (the `π • p` and `π • q` membership arguments) and the two `exists_mul_self_sub_mem_span_and_sub_mem` calls are also short and differ in sign or type. The helper lemmas `isNilpotent_mk_of_mem_map`, `map_mul_self_sub_mem_span` and `map_mem_map_maximalIdeal` are already factored out. I found no nontrivial reasoning duplicated across proofs. I am uncertain only about the borderline idempotent-block repetition described above.
